title: Executable Images and OS Loading
description: Follow a program from an executable image to its first instruction: the kernel's mapping, the auxiliary vector, the initial stack and the addresses you are handed.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 6 concepts, reproduce the 41 measured checks in courses/img/assets/samples/crosscheck.py, and run courses/img/assets/samples/stackwalk.py

concepts.title: The Auxiliary Vector
concepts.description: The third array on the initial stack, the one no C library function will give you.

concepts.title: Reading the Initial Stack by Hand
concepts.description: argc, argv, envp, auxv as raw bytes, and the off-by-one that segfaults.

concepts.title: What Each Entry Is For
concepts.description: The three that matter, the arithmetic that ties them to the file, and the pointer-versus-size trap.

concepts.title: The vDSO: An ELF File With No File
concepts.description: A shared library the kernel synthesises, maps into every process, and backs with nothing.

concepts.title: Where the Kernel Put Everything
concepts.description: The process map, the 64 KB floor, and why a hint is not a request.

concepts.title: Rebuilding the Image Reader
concepts.description: Read the raw stack, decode it with no libc, and check every value against the file and against procfs.
